about: Ensembl (ensembl.org) genome browser: search thousands of genome assemblies, read genome metadata and stats, look up genes, transcripts, proteins, homologues, external references and variants (with predicted consequences), and fetch reference sequence through Ensembl's public JSON and GraphQL APIs.

commands.summary: Search genome assemblies by name. Can list every assembly of one species by taxonomy id, and can sort (e.g. by contig N50) and paginate.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text search: common name, scientific name or assembly name/accession

params.name: species_taxonomy_id
params.description: NCBI species taxonomy id. Restricts results to all assemblies of that species (e.g. 9606 = human, 10090 = mouse)

params.name: sort
params.description: Field to sort by, e.g. contig_n50. Omit for relevance ranking

commands.summary: Download genome search results as CSV text, matching search-genomes for the same query.

params.name: species_taxonomy_id
params.description: NCBI species taxonomy id that restricts the export to one species' assemblies

commands.summary: Get metadata for one genome by its UUID: assembly, providers, annotation version/date, release and reference status.
Get statistics for a genome: assembly (N50, length, GC%), coding, non-coding, pseudogene and variation counts.
Get example gene, location and variant ids for a genome. These are handy starting points for gene and variant lookups.
List popular species with their taxonomy id and number of available genomes.
List genome group categories, such as external projects like VGP and BGE, with genome counts.
Get the total number of genomes in Ensembl and the count per taxonomic group (Animals, Archaea, …).
List Ensembl data releases (name, type integrated/partial, is_current).
Search genes by symbol, name or stable id within one genome. Returns stable ids, biotype and location.

params.name: query
params.description: Gene symbol, name or Ensembl stable id

params.name: genome_id
params.description: Genome UUID to search in (default: Human GRCh38.p14)

commands.summary: Search variants (e.g. by rsID) within one genome.
Get a gene's versioned stable id, symbol, chromosome location, strand and biotype.

params.name: geneId
params.description: Ensembl gene stable id (unversioned ok), e.g. ENSG00000139618

commands.summary: Get a gene's full name, alternative symbols (synonyms), HGNC accession and biotype.
Get a gene's transcripts with exon layout, CDS coordinates, protein product ids and canonical/MANE flags. This is what the feature explorer gene view draws.
List all transcripts of a gene with biotype, length, canonical/MANE status and protein length. Also returns the gene location and region checksum.
Get cross-references (NCBI Gene, HGNC, OMIM, GeneCards, UniProt, RefSeq, …) for a gene and for each of its transcripts and proteins.
List homologues/orthologues of a gene in other species, with homology type and percent identity/coverage.

params.name: geneId
params.description: Versioned Ensembl gene stable id, e.g. ENSG00000139618.19 (use stable_id from get-gene-summary)

commands.summary: Get one transcript's location, exons, CDS coordinates and protein product (id, length, sequence checksum).

params.name: transcriptId
params.description: Versioned Ensembl transcript stable id, e.g. ENST00000366667.6

commands.summary: Get a protein's length and its domain/family matches (Pfam, PANTHER, InterPro, …) with positions.

params.name: productId
params.description: Versioned Ensembl protein stable id, e.g. ENSP00000369497.3

commands.summary: Get PDBe summary counts for a UniProt accession: number of PDB structures, ligands, interaction partners and similar proteins.
Get variant details: location, alleles, allele type, dbSNP source, VEP prediction, citation count, phenotype assertions and population allele frequencies.

params.name: variantId
params.description: Variant id in the form {chromosome}:{position}:{rsID}, e.g. 1:230710048:rs699

commands.summary: Get the predicted molecular consequences of each allele of a variant on overlapping transcripts: consequence terms plus cDNA, CDS and protein positions with ref/alt.
Get a chromosome/region's length, topology and sequence checksum. Use the checksum with get-sequence.
Fetch raw DNA or protein sequence (plain text) for a sequence checksum over a coordinate range, via refget. Uses 0-based start and exclusive end.

params.name: checksum
params.description: Sequence checksum: a region checksum from get-region, or a protein sequence checksum from get-transcript

params.name: start
params.description: 0-based start coordinate (inclusive). For a 1-based genomic position P, use P-1. Example: 230710027 for a variant flank

params.name: end
params.description: End coordinate (exclusive, 0-based). Equals the 1-based inclusive end. Length returned = end - start
